findings.finding: B2's blocking predicate is built on plan_review_status/claim_gate_check, which verifies a plan-review attestation ONLY against the verifying host's OWN environment key. Any attestation signed by a different principal (the normal case for a review-bot host distinct from the developer who ran review-plan) returns verdict 'foreign_key' (HMAC signing.py:401-419; op-cert _opcert_signing.py:470-488) or 'mismatch' (HMAC signed-elsewhere, signing.py:432-439), WITHOUT reaching the cross-environment keyring/era trust-root path (opcert.py:246-320) the merge-gate uses. The plan buckets foreign_key/mismatch as FLAG -> BLOCK. Therefore a legitimately-reviewed, certified oversized bug fix will be BLOCKED on the review-bot host, inverting the gate's purpose.

Re-bucket keyless-host/no-trust-root outcomes into INFRA-FAIL-OPEN (advisory), and add an integration test where the fixture attestation's principal differs from the review-bot's own principal to prove a certified cross-host plan is ACCEPTED, not blocked.
